title: The modules an app is composed of are not decided under a condition
intent: An app is composed from a list of modules, and the access check records who can reach each route by composing the app wherever the check runs. A module added to that list under a condition (an environment variable, a setting, whether an object is absent) is mounted where the condition holds and nowhere else, so the app serves routes in one environment that the check, run in another, never saw: the surface a reviewer approved is not the surface deployed. The rule follows the list the composition is handed back through the file that builds it and refuses each place it is decided under a condition: a conditional expression among its elements, a change to it under a branch, a loop or an error handler, a comprehension or a filter that drops elements, a helper that returns it under a condition, and the same through a parameter to the function's callers in that file. The compliant form mounts the module always and lets its routes refuse while it is not configured.
reference: create_app([login_module, me_module, oidc_module], ...) with every module named in every environment; a module whose configuration is per environment is built always (build_oidc_module(providers, ..., allow_no_provider=True)) and answers a typed refusal while it has none.

runtime.rationale: The invariant survives into the running system as its consequence: the routes the composed app serves either are or are not the ones the committed authorization surface records. The source scan reads one file, so a list built in another module, or a module object that is itself None under a condition, is outside it; a fail-closed comparison at startup of the composed routes with the shipped authz-surface.json would catch those, and every other way the served surface can differ from the recorded one. The framework owns that seam (create_app, after composition) and has not shipped the control: it runs the app's own code against its own record, which is a decision recorded as open.
runtime.tracking: terp-framework ADR 0209, Open (whether the access check may keep running the app's own code), and ADR 0211: the startup self-check in terp.core.app that compares the composed routes with the authz-surface.json the image carries and refuses to start on a difference.
